clue.text: One politician with paper runners obstructed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard politician
the people who run a newspaper are editors, each abbreviated ED, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A politician teams up with newspaper staff to block something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper runners' is plural, so two editors (ED twice) close the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder or block, so obstructed and impeded are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: High flier dropped from the Sun for not listening to pop

definitions.text: High flier dropped from the Sun for not listening to pop

parts.words: High flier dropped from the Sun for not listening to pop
parts.note: the Greek myth of the boy who ignored his father's warning and flew so close to the sun that his wax wings melted and he fell

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Sun' looks like the British tabloid and 'pop' like music; pop is his father Daedalus.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical boy who soared on waxed wings and fell when the sun melted them fits the description.

clue.text: Naked boy's clothing was profitable for cashier

indicators.note: clothing means the cherub word is wrapped round the profit word

parts.note: a putto is a naked cherub in Renaissance art
something that paid was profitable

explanation.surface: A naked lad's outfit made money for the bank teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' is a verb here: to dismiss or end.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss, especially from the forces; putting paid to something ends it the same way.

clue.text: Having power to upset a lot of detectives?

indicators.note: upset means the combined letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a lot of means many
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, detectives

explanation.surface: Is it a sign of strength to annoy a great number of police investigators?
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means forceful and full of energy, possessing power.

clue.text: Fish page left in dish

indicators.note: in places the page word inside the dish word

parts.note: to dish out is to dole out
the verso is the left-hand page of a book

explanation.surface: A recipe page left beside a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like a plate of food but is a verb, as in dish out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dover sole is a European flatfish prized for eating.

clue.text: One getting immediate lift from spring beside fountain

parts.note: to spring is to leap or bound
a fountain throws up a spout or stream of water

explanation.surface: Something gets an instant boost by leaping up beside a water feature.
explanation.walkthrough: A jump jet is an aircraft such as the Harrier that takes off vertically, with no runway run-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertical take-off aircraft rise straight up the moment they start, so their lift is immediate.

clue.text: Male judge not right for laws initially

indicators.note: not with initially says the right letter is dropped from the start of the laws word
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs

parts.note: rules are laws

explanation.surface: A man on the bench rejects correctness as the first principle of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' looks like a description of the judge, but it is the definition: a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules is a man's first name, as in Jules Verne, so it names a male.

clue.text: American racing to fit in second university qualification

indicators.note: to fit in places the racing word inside the second word

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
IndyCar is the American motor-racing series

explanation.surface: An American race driver needs a degree to get a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualification' is not a degree but a qualifying remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a reservation to what was just said, a spoken qualification.

clue.text: May successor with army form it?

definitions.text: May successor with army form it?

parts.note: June follows May, abbreviated JUN
TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Will Theresa May's successor team up with the military to set up a government?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a military regime that seizes power after an earlier ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a military group that takes power, forming a government with the army.

clue.text: Cylinder found among sets thrown out of planes?

indicators.note: found among places the cylinder inside the rearranged letters
thrown means the letters of sets are tossed into a new order

parts.note: a reel is a cylinder for winding

explanation.surface: A cylinder turns up among scattered sets ejected from aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planes' are plane trees, not aircraft, so 'out of planes' means having none of those trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes are trees, so a place out of them has no trees at all.

clue.text: An unusually violent literary genre

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of violent appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A new kind of book full of brutality.
explanation.definitionFit: The antinovel is a form of experimental fiction rejecting conventional plot and character, a recognised literary type.

clue.text: Design on cent piece coined for special occasion

indicators.note: piece says the answer is a piece of the run of words design on cent

explanation.surface: A pattern is minted on part of a coin for a commemorative issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in order across the end of design, all of on and the start of cent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is one made up for a single particular use, the coinage serving one occasion only.

clue.text: Neutralise defence of football team containing right back

indicators.note: back says the combined letters are read from end to start
containing places the right abbreviation inside the team name

parts.note: Man U is the short name for Manchester United football club

explanation.surface: A football side, with a right-back in it, has its defence nullified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' looks like a football position; 'right' goes inside MANU to give MRANU, which 'back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm is to take away weapons, which neutralises any defence someone could offer.

clue.text: One driven home in poor condition after drinking it?

definitions.text: One driven home in poor condition after drinking it?

parts.words: One driven home in poor condition after drinking it?
parts.note: a corroded fastener is hammered into wood, and it is also the name of a Scotch and Drambuie cocktail that leaves the drinker the worse for wear

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: a corroded spike hammered in, and a whisky cocktail whose drinker may end up in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an old corroded spike and a cocktail of Scotch whisky with Drambuie.

clue.text: Lace securely tied by American binding posh character in old drama

parts.note: to lace a drink is to spike or doctor it

indicators.note: binding means the securely tied word wraps round the posh letter

parts.note: something securely tied is fast
U is the old label for upper-class usage, hence posh

explanation.surface: Someone ties a lace firmly while an American restrains a toff in a period play.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe's Elizabethan tragedy is named after its hero, the scholar who sells his soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe's tragic hero is the central figure of an Elizabethan play, a character in old drama.

clue.text: Settles on sack after lifting small item of furniture

parts.note: to foot a bill is to settle it

indicators.note: after lifting puts the reversed sack word after, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: Someone sits down on a bag after picking it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settles' looks like the bench but is the verb, as in settles the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool for resting the feet, a small piece of furniture.

clue.text: It follows you round touching behind!

indicators.note: round means the you word goes about the other two

parts.note: thee is the old word for you
re means about or concerning, touching on
to be behind someone is to be for them

explanation.surface: It trails after you, putting a hand on your bottom!
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' as in backing someone gives its supporter word; 'touching' means concerning, not physical contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore introduces a conclusion that follows from what came before.

clue.text: Shiny silver paper discarded

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
discarded paper is litter

explanation.surface: Bright silver paper is thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering or sparkling, so it describes something shiny.

clue.text: Eg poor Grieg composition that is one not to play after upsetting girls

definitions.text: one not to play after upsetting girls

indicators.note: a musical composition puts the notes together, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clumsy arrangement of a Grieg piece, presented as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme he kissed the girls and made them cry, and when the boys came out to play he ran away.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's boy upset the girls with kisses and then fled rather than join the boys at play.

clue.text: One's content to stick leg out, mischievously keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the quiet letter
mischievously says the letters of leg out are set out in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Someone happy to trip people up by sticking a leg out, keeping silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick leg out' reads as tripping someone; 'to stick' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A glue pot is a container whose contents are for sticking things together.

clue.text: Trinity student driving away from Normandy beach with teacher

indicators.note: driving away from says the student letter leaves the beach name

parts.note: Gold was one of the D-Day landing beaches in Normandy
L is the learner plate abbreviation for student
a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A Trinity College student drives off from a French beach with a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity' looks like the Cambridge college; it is the Christian Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godhead is the divine nature of God, in Christian doctrine the Trinity of three persons.

clue.text: Belgian place mat smothered in cream, mostly

indicators.note: smothered in means the mat word goes inside the cream word
mostly says the cream word loses its last letter

parts.note: the cream is the best
a rug is a mat

explanation.surface: A doormat is drowned in cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' is the best of anything, not dairy; 'mostly' trims its last letter before the mat goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruges is a canal city in Flanders, a place in Belgium.

clue.text: Novel company about to praise us

indicators.note: about means the company name goes round the praise word

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a famous British company
to laud is to praise
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new company is set up to sing our praises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for company but is the definition: Robert Graves's book about the Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves's 1934 book narrated by the Roman emperor is a famous historical novel.

clue.text: Police stick note on this when son goes missing

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: when son goes missing says the S abbreviation for son is dropped

explanation.surface: Police put a notice on this baton, with a boy gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is the long bamboo truncheon of Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a lathi is a heavy stick carried as a weapon by the police.

clue.text: Port is unadulterated, we understand

indicators.note: we understand signals that the words are heard, not seen

parts.note: mere means pure, nothing more, so is unadulterated suggests is mere

explanation.surface: This fortified wine is pure, we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine; it is a harbour city in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a major seaport on Turkey's Aegean coast.

clue.text: Dull having organ to pick up on way back

indicators.note: on says the organ word is placed on, after, the turned-round way in the across entry
back says the way abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the ear is the organ that picks up sounds

explanation.surface: Something boring involves an organ to collect on the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning gloomy or dull.

clue.text: Reckon infant's bedtime over?

parts.note: a tot is a small child
when bedtime is over, you are up

explanation.surface: Work out when the small child's bedtime finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue says the tot's time is up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add up a total, which is to reckon a sum.

clue.text: Revolutionary and confusing passages about old character from Lear

indicators.note: about means the passages word goes round the old letter

parts.note: a maze is a confusing network of passages
the Dong with a Luminous Nose is a creature from Edward Lear's nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A rebel caught in a bewildering network of tunnels around a figure from Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lear here is Edward Lear the nonsense poet, not Shakespeare's king.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao led the Chinese communist revolution, so he is a famous revolutionary.

clue.text: One schedule is gripping — and large it emerges

indicators.note: is gripping means the schedule holds the one letter inside it

parts.note: a roster is a duty schedule
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A timetable grips someone, and partying comes out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large it' is British slang for partying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, the same as the slang for having a wild night out.

clue.text: Runs lots of steps

definitions.meaning: runs are the vertical splits in stockings or tights
sets of rungs or steps for climbing

explanation.definitionFit: Ladders are both snags in hosiery, in British usage, and frameworks of rungs to climb.
